field.label: Host names
field.help: The names this site is reached by, as a browser asks for them: www.example.com, or a wildcard for every name under a domain, *.example.com. The first is the site's own name. A host name belongs to one site: none may be another site's, or under another site's wildcard. A request for a name no site has is refused, and not inspected.

field.label: Backend
field.help: The site's own server, which its inspected requests are passed to: http:// or https://, an address or a name, a port, and a path where the site is not at the server's root - http://192.0.2.10:8080 or https://intranet.example.com/app. The host name a browser asked for is passed on as it is: an https:// backend is asked for that name too, and its certificate is checked against it.

field.label: Check the backend's certificate
field.help: For an https:// backend: its certificate must be signed by an authority of this firewall's trust store and be valid for the site's host names, not for the name or address written in Backend - the name the browser asked for is passed on, and asked of the backend (SNI). A backend whose certificate names only itself: turn this off. Off: any certificate is taken - only for a server on a network you trust.

field.label: Certificate
field.help: The site's certificate of System: Trust, with its private key: the site is then served over HTTPS, and its plain HTTP requests are sent there. None: the site is served over plain HTTP.

field.label: Mode
field.help: Detection only: every request is inspected and what the rules find is logged, and the request passes - the first mode of a new site, to see what the rules would refuse before they refuse it. Blocking: a request the rules judge an attack is refused with 403. So is, at every level, a method other than GET, HEAD, POST and OPTIONS - a WebDAV or REST backend's PUT, DELETE or PROPFIND - or a content type the Core Rule Set does not list: keep such a site in Detection only. And in Blocking a request body larger than 12.5 MiB with files, or 128 KiB without, is refused with 413.

field.label: Paranoia level
field.help: How many of the Core Rule Set's rules run: 1 has the fewest false positives and suits most sites; each level up adds rules that find more attacks, and refuse more ordinary requests. Raise it after the site has run in Detection only at it.
